study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Tabbal et al., npj Parkinson's Disease, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of neurodegenerative diseases through EEG normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states its objectives: (1) build normative trajectories for EEG features in healthy controls over 40; (2) use individual-level deviation scores from normative models to map heterogeneity in AD and PD. These directly satisfy that research questions/purpose are described and the purpose of applying normative modeling is made explicit.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "In this study, we utilized normative models and EEG data from 14 datasets to achieve two primary objectives. First, we aimed to chart the trajectory of standard EEG features... in a cohort of healthy control (HC) individuals over 40 years old (yo). Second, we leveraged individual-level inferences from the normative models to map the heterogeneity within AD and PD groups."
cm1_research_objectives.location: Tabbal2025.pdf.md: 33-39 (see block starting 'In this study, we utilized normative models...')

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This is a NEW normative model. Inclusion is described (healthy controls aged >40, eyes-closed resting EEG; multi-site aggregation). Image/data quality procedures are specified (automated preprocessing including bandpass filters, downsampling, bad channel detection, ICA, Autoreject). Final HC sample sizes are reported (400 train, 99 held-out). Reasons for exclusion are not detailed for the HC reference cohort; explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond age and health status are limited.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Resting-state eyes-closed EEG data was collected from subjects aged 40 to 92 years, across 14 sites... Normative models were trained on 400 (46% M) HC participants while 99 (42% M) HC participants were held out..."; "The EEG preprocessing and artifact removal pipeline... bandpass filtering (1–100 Hz)... downsampled... bad EEG channels were identified using the pyprep algorithm... ICA... Autoreject toolbox was used to detect and clean or reject bad epochs."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are considered as covariates within the GAMLSS models (sex included at least for delta-band connectivity; age modeled across bands). The study uses multi-site data and addresses site variation via LOSO sensitivity analysis and harmonized channel mapping, but does not include site as an explicit covariate nor apply a harmonization method like ComBat; site-effect handling is discussed as a limitation.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "The optimal distribution family, model parameters ... and covariates are indicated in Supplementary Tables 4 and 5."; "mu: y ~ fp(age, 1) + factor(sex) ... sigma: ~ fp(age, 1)..."; "we ran a leave-one-study-out analysis... no specific dataset significantly influenced NM trajectories"; "Future research should explore advanced harmonization techniques, such as Combat family methods..."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data sources for the reference cohort are described and enumerated across 14 studies with details provided in Supplementary Data 1/2, including dataset/study names, sites, and references.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The data were aggregated from 14 distinct studies... A detailed overview of the datasets ... is provided in Supplementary Data 1."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is detailed: bandpass filters, downsampling, notch filter, bad channel detection with pyprep (RANSAC), rereferencing, ICA with ICLabel, Autoreject for epoch cleaning, and special handling for an already preprocessed dataset. Software/toolboxes are named.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The EEG preprocessing and artifact removal pipeline... bandpass filtering (1–100 Hz)... downsampled ... notch filter... bad EEG channels... pyprep ... rereferencing... ICA ... ICLabel ... A second bandpass filter (1–45 Hz) ... segmented into 10-s epochs ... Autoreject toolbox..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The HC cohort was split into a training set (N=400) and a held-out test set (N=99). Additionally, a leave-one-study-out (LOSO) analysis was performed to test sensitivity to site/dataset.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Normative models were trained on 400 (46% M) HC participants while 99 (42% M) HC participants were held out..."; "The model sensitivity was analyzed with a leave-one-study-out (LOSO) analysis."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: There is no application of the normative model to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals beyond the aggregated multi-site data; validation uses an internal hold-out and LOSO, not a separate external cohort.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No text describes evaluation on an external independent HC dataset; validation is described as held-out HC(test) and LOSO within the aggregated datasets.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: GAMLSS models per feature and band; identification of optimal distribution family and parameters; covariates specified; software specified (gamlss in R).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "we implemented the Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS) using the gamlss package... We started by identifying the optimal data distribution and best-fitting parameters and covariates."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is assessed qualitatively via convergence, residuals, and Q–Q plots, and robustness via LOSO, but no explicit quantitative fit metrics (e.g., R^2, coverage) are reported in text.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The model performance was assessed by the model convergence, residuals, and Q–Q (quantile-quantile) plots. The model sensitivity was analyzed with a leave-one-study-out (LOSO) analysis."
